title: Starting over before I lose my mind. What tech stack are you guys actually using to build bots?
author: Shani-_-
selftext:
After spending way too much time fighting execution quirks, weird broker headaches, and my own questionable code, I am hitting pause and rethinking my entire setup.

​Before I sink another month into reinventing the wheel, I want to know what a sane, reliable stack actually looks like in the real world.

​If you have a setup that runs without making you want to throw your monitor out the window:

1. ​What language and core libraries are you using? (Python with CCXT, C#, C++, Rust, etc.?)

2. ​Framework or from scratch? (NautilusTrader, QuantConnect/Lean, Hummingbot, or custom roll-your-own?)

3. ​How are you handling execution? (Direct exchange REST/WebSockets, or routing through something like MT4/MT5, TradingView webhooks, etc.?)

4. ​Do you use the same environment for backtesting and live execution, or two completely different tools?

5. ​Where do you host it? (Basic cheap VPS, AWS/GCP, or a dedicated machine?)

Curious where most people land between "keep it dead simple with a Python script on a VPS" and "full-blown mini hedge fund infrastructure."

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body:
I run my platform on Hyperliquid. I have two Leaseweb #6 VPS's, one to host the app and one for my own non validator HL node, both in the same data center in Tokyo (since HL is in Japan).

Stack:

Next.js
FastAPI
Postgres
Redis
Custom worker

You can run a bot for free, forever on my platform if you're interested in AI trading. It is fully open, customizable, inspectable, and all settings, trades and results are shared. You can also do deep analytics with your coding harness (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)

It works with free Gemma 4 models on Google AI Studio API or you can connect Codex, Claude Code, etc and use your subsidized accounts for inference or run the bot in fully agentic mode.

I'm running 22 bots myself, 10 on Gemma 4 and 12 with GPT 5.6 Sol High which I'm planning to switch to GPT 6 Astra to check if it's visible usage wise. Most of my users use free Gemma 4 31B models.

replies.author: NefariousnessOpening
replies.body: You definitely just had something missing. Generally though transformers are ok at some aspects of trading but they don’t have a sense of time or the detriment of temporal reasoning. Trading is based around a lot of time series data from a model perspective. Try some other models. I’ve been using models that are 500MB up to 2-4GB and they are very fast for sure but also have the temporal edge. RL is a bit less overhead for the workload, less data is needed to fine tune

comments.author: Much-Section-7680
comments.body:
I went pretty much full custom at this point.

Python backend, FastAPI, React/TS/Vite frontend. No QuantConnect, Hummingbot etc.

But honestly most of the architecture is just infrastructure to make the AI agents happy lol.

The agents themselves run through LLM APIs, have tools to pull market data / account state / execute trades, and a few different memory layers between runs. So they can basically work in their own little world, keep context, learn stuff, wake themselves up again when something interesting happens, etc.

One thing I do in basically all my agent projects is give every agent a defined output state.

So internally they can reason, use memory, call tools, whatever. But what the human sees is always a clean structured block like:

state  
bias  
regime  
what it's watching  
confidence  
headline / rationale

Makes the frontend way easier because I don't have to somehow turn 20k tokens of agent rambling into a UI. The agent already has to tell me what actually matters.

Execution is direct exchange API/WebSockets. Hosting is just a server, nothing exotic.

So yeah... somewhere between "Python script on a VPS" and "accidentally built a tiny hedge fund infrastructure."

If you want to see what that looks like in practice: [https://soulquant.ai](https://soulquant.ai)
